projects.title: Beyond OS
projects.description: A centralized business operating system that unifies CRM, HRMS, projects, approvals, and reporting in one configurable enterprise app.
projects.overview: Designed and built a Business Operating System that pulls CRM, HRMS, project management, approvals, employee records, and reporting into a single configurable platform. Modular architecture so a new organization can be onboarded without rebuilding the product.
whoFor: Ops leads tired of CRM, HR, and projects living in different spreadsheets
Founders who need one internal system instead of a tool stack
Admins onboarding multiple organizations without custom rebuilds

modules.title: Unified CRM
modules.detail: Accounts, contacts, and pipeline in the same system as the rest of operations.

modules.title: HRMS & employees
modules.detail: Employee records and admin workflows sitting next to the work, not in a side tool.

modules.title: Projects & approvals
modules.detail: Configurable approval chains so work does not stall in inboxes and chats.

modules.title: Org reporting
modules.detail: A single view of teams, projects, and operational performance.

modules.title: RBAC
modules.detail: Granular roles so each org can expose only the modules a user should see.

modules.title: Multi-tenant config
modules.detail: Reusable components and org settings instead of forking the product per customer.

workflow.title: Configure the org
workflow.detail: Stand up the tenant with modules, branding, and baseline settings.

workflow.title: Assign roles
workflow.detail: Map people to RBAC so CRM, HR, and admin stay correctly scoped.

workflow.title: Run the work
workflow.detail: Projects, approvals, and employee workflows happen in one place.

workflow.title: Report across modules
workflow.detail: Leadership sees operational performance without exporting five tools.

problemPoints: Business operations were spread across disconnected tools and spreadsheets.
Manual approvals and repetitive admin work slowed teams down.
Limited visibility into teams, projects, and operational performance.
Scaling to new organizations meant repeated customization.
decisionPoints: Modular architecture so business modules can ship independently.
Role-based access control for granular permissions.
Configurable workflows, approvals, and organization settings.
API-first so web, mobile, and integrations share one core.
Reusable components and centralized config for future expansion.
outcomePoints: Multiple business functions now live on one platform.
Less operational overhead through workflow automation.
Faster org onboarding with configuration instead of custom builds.
A reusable enterprise base for AI assistants, analytics, and more modules.
next: An AI ops assistant on top of the same records and workflows.
More plug-in modules without rewriting the core.

projects.title: Beyond C
projects.description: A creator marketplace and campaign workspace that centralizes discovery, messaging, tracking, and analytics for brands, creators, and agencies.
projects.overview: Beyond C is a creator marketplace and campaign platform built to un-fragment influencer marketing. Discovery, communication, campaign tracking, and analytics sit in one product so brands, creators, and agencies can actually finish a campaign together.
whoFor: Brands hunting creators who match audience and campaign goals
Creators who need a real pipeline instead of cold DMs
Agencies juggling multiple clients, creators, and campaigns

modules.title: Creator discovery
modules.detail: Filter by category, audience, and performance instead of spreadsheet hunts.

modules.title: Campaign workspace
modules.detail: Briefs, status, and ownership live in one dashboard per role.

modules.title: In-app messaging
modules.detail: Replace WhatsApp / email / DM scatter with a single thread.

modules.title: Milestones & agreements
modules.detail: Digital agreements and checkpoints so work is visible and accountable.

modules.title: Campaign analytics
modules.detail: Track creator and campaign effectiveness without a side spreadsheet.

modules.title: Role dashboards
modules.detail: Brand, creator, and agency each get a workflow that matches how they work.

workflow.title: Discover
workflow.detail: Find creators against audience and campaign goals.

workflow.title: Brief the campaign
workflow.detail: Spin up a workspace with roles, deliverables, and agreements.

workflow.title: Collaborate
workflow.detail: Message, ship assets, and hit milestones in one product.

workflow.title: Measure
workflow.detail: Read performance and decide who to work with next.

problemPoints: Brands struggled to find creators who matched audience and goals.
Campaign comms were scattered across WhatsApp, email, sheets, and DMs.
Manual campaign ops meant missed deadlines and no shared visibility.
Smaller creators had no clean path to brand work.
Agencies had no single workspace for clients, creators, and campaigns.

decisionPoints: One SaaS connecting brands, creators, and agencies.

Messaging, campaign ops, and collaboration in the same product.

projects.title: Linkedin Automator
projects.description: An AI content platform that drafts, schedules, and publishes LinkedIn posts so a consistent presence does not eat the week.
projects.overview: An AI-powered platform for LinkedIn content creation, scheduling, and publishing. It is built for people and teams who need a consistent presence without writing every post from scratch or hopping between calendars and analytics.
whoFor: Operators who need a LinkedIn cadence without a content team
Founders who want on-brand posts from a prompt, not a blank page
Agencies and teams managing more than one LinkedIn account

modules.title: AI drafts from a prompt
modules.detail: Turn a short idea into a post instead of staring at a blank composer.

modules.title: Calendar + publish
modules.detail: Schedule and ship through a content calendar instead of last-minute posting.

modules.title: Templates & tone
modules.detail: Reusable structures and tone so the feed still sounds like the person.

modules.title: Multi-account dashboard
modules.detail: Run more than one LinkedIn presence from a single workspace.

modules.title: Performance analytics
modules.detail: See what landed so the next batch is not a guess.

modules.title: Team review
modules.detail: A path for review and approval before anything goes live.

workflow.title: Prompt

workflow.title: Generate

workflow.title: Learn
workflow.detail: Read analytics and feed the next round of prompts.

problemPoints: A consistent LinkedIn presence is time-consuming to maintain.

Quality writing still takes real effort.
Multiple LinkedIn accounts are painful to run by hand.

Scheduling across time zones is clumsy.

A calendar with automated scheduling and publishing.
Templates and tone controls for different audiences.
Analytics to steer the next batch of content.
One dashboard for multiple LinkedIn accounts.
Collaboration so teams can review before publish.

More consistent posting without living in the composer.
Planning happens in a calendar, not a chat thread.
Personal branding can scale across multiple profiles.

next: Stronger approval flows for agencies and teams.
Richer performance loops back into generation.

cta.heading: Hiring a product-minded builder?
cta.description: I'd rather chat than send another cold DM. Book a call, drop an email, or just say hi.

bio: I'm Vaibhav — senior software engineer with 3+ years of full-stack experience across the .NET and JavaScript worlds. I've spent most of that time in the enterprise trenches, shipping React and Next.js frontends onto .NET Core and Azure backends, and picking up MERN/MEAN work along the way.

Somewhere in the last 18 months, my curiosity outgrew the ticket queue. I started building AI tools for myself on nights and weekends — four of them, so far — and each one taught me that the hard part was never the code. It was scoping, sequencing, and knowing what not to build.

That's the muscle I want to grow next. I'm spending more time where the code meets the user — not because engineering bored me, but because the most interesting decisions in AI products live one layer up: what to build, for whom, with what tradeoffs, at what pace. That's the room I'm earning a seat in.

timeline.title: Started as a .NET engineer
timeline.description: Joined the enterprise trenches — .NET Core, Azure, MERN/MEAN. Learned that shipping is a team sport and that most production bugs live in the seams between systems, not the systems themselves.

timeline.title: Went full-stack + cloud
timeline.description: Owned end-to-end features across React, Next.js, and Azure. Got the Cloud Computing Architecture cert. Started asking 'why are we building this?' more often than 'how do we build this?'.

timeline.title: The AI switch flipped
timeline.description: Fell hard for the modern AI stack — Claude Code, n8n, ComfyUI, Ollama, ElevenLabs. Realized my engineering superpower isn't code, it's shipping the thing end-to-end while everyone else prototypes.

timeline.title: Built 4 AI tools solo
timeline.description: LinkedIn Automator, Idea Curator, Leads Finder, Agentic Workflow Summarizer — all self-initiated, all documented as case studies. Earned the PM certification along the way.

timeline.title: Betting on product-led engineering
timeline.description: Widening my lane from 'how to build' to 'what to build, for whom, and why now' — where engineering context, AI intuition, and product judgment overlap. It's where the interesting decisions get made.
